text: This bond wears its conversation on the outside. Whatever else these two do together, the talking is the visible part, and it is what other people mention first when they describe the pair. Composite Mercury in the first house puts the relationship's mind where its face is. How this relationship sounds is how it is known. The standing subject is the bond itself. These two define it, redefine it, and narrate it: how it started, what to call it, what it is like from inside, whether it has changed since last year. That is not vanity. It is how the pair keeps track of where it stands, and the conversation runs for years without finishing. A version of the origin story gets told to almost everyone they meet, and the telling improves with use. Because the talk sits at the front, this relationship thinks out loud rather than in private. Opinions get formed in company and reported afterwards. Other people find the pair easy to approach and easy to overhear. Decisions made in front of an audience tend to hold better here than the ones the two of you reach alone in a car. The limit of the placement is that the frame rarely widens. A conversation this interested in itself has less room for the subject that has nothing to do with either person. Whole regions of the world can go undiscussed, not from lack of curiosity but because the nearer subject keeps arriving first, and the nearer subject is always these two.

Money comes up early here, and it keeps coming up. A second-house Mercury sets this pair's conversation on the subject of worth: what things cost, what each brings, what is held and by whom, what a plan would take to do properly. This says nothing about how much there is. It says where the talk lands. Practical accounting becomes a shared language. These two can spend an evening on numbers the way another pair spends one on a film, and neither treats it as a chore. Decisions get made by pricing them out. A trip, a move, a piece of furniture: each gets weighed aloud, and the weighing is half the pleasure. The result is real competence with resources and plans that survive contact with the actual figures. The habit spreads past money. Effort gets counted. Time gets counted. What one did last month and what the other did in return can be tallied in the same tone used for a bill, and fairness is a live question in this bond rather than an assumption. It gets raised often, sometimes as a joke that is only half joking. Possessions are ordinary subjects too, along with skills, along with anything else that makes the pair feel steady. Security is discussed here rather than simply felt. Both are quick to notice when the ground moves, and quicker to say so. What sits outside the frame is the thing with no price on it. A subject that cannot be weighed against something else tends to get set down half said. Grief, a mood with no cause, an attachment that makes no sense on paper: those are harder to carry into a conversation built for comparison. An hour can go on a sum of money when the matter underneath was something neither of you could put a figure on at all.

Errands, messages, a link sent at eleven at night: the ordinary traffic between these two is heavy. This is Mercury's own house, and a composite Mercury sitting in it produces volume. Words are the medium the relationship runs on, and there is a constant low exchange going on about nothing much. The nothing much is what holds the days together. Subjects come from close by: the street, the commute, whoever lives on the other side of the wall, the relatives who turn up often enough to have a running storyline. Brothers, sisters and cousins get more airtime here than in most bonds, whatever shape those families take. Short journeys are talking occasions, and the pair takes them: the drive, the walk to the shop, the twenty minutes to the station. Information moves fast and accurately in this relationship. A change of plan reaches the other person quickly, little is lost on the way, and neither of you spends much time finding out too late. Practical coordination is close to effortless. The pair also writes to each other more than most. Messages pile up into a record, and the record gets quoted back. A shorthand develops early, made of half-words and references, and it becomes almost impossible to explain to anyone outside it. One piece of housekeeping belongs in this entry, because the whole reading stands on an address. A composite chart has no horizon of its own. Its houses are counted in twelve equal steps from a degree halfway between the two Ascendants, and this cell is the third step in that count. The count is a convention, and it rests on both birth times being recorded accurately. If the heavy traffic described here is nothing like the traffic between you, doubt the arithmetic before the description. What the register does not do is climb. Everything is available and everything stays at one altitude. A serious subject enters the stream, gets three sentences, and is carried along with the rest of it. Neither person is refusing the subject. The format simply has no gear for stopping. So years of unbroken contact can go by with the one conversation both would call important still waiting its turn. When it does arrive, it arrives in the same casual voice as everything else, usually in a car or a corridor or halfway through something else, and then the traffic picks up again behind it.

Most of what gets said here gets said indoors. The fourth house draws the pair's talk toward home, family, and what came before, so this relationship sounds different in private than it does anywhere else. In company these two may be unremarkable. Behind a door of their own, the conversation opens. The standing subjects are the ones a shared base generates, and a shared base need not mean one address: what a place requires, who is coming to stay, how a room ought to work, what each grew up with. Comparing those two childhoods is a long project in this bond. It never quite ends, because every new situation turns up another difference nobody thought to mention. Memory is active. Old conversations get quoted accurately and often. The pair keeps a shared record of its own history and consults it, and a disagreement about what happened in a room three years ago can take an entire evening. Neither is being difficult about it. The record matters to both of you, and it is not identical in either head. Talk also does household work. Plans get made sitting down, in a familiar place, with something to drink. This is not a relationship that thinks well on the move or in public, and asking it to decide something in a restaurant tends to produce a decision that gets revisited at home. What stays outside is the wider world. The pair's attention is domestic, and public matters can go weeks without being raised. This bond can be very well informed about its own small circle and only vaguely informed about anything past it. That is the direction the talk falls rather than a narrowness of mind, and whatever this pair assembles gets assembled inward, one room at a time.

Between these two, talking is something done for enjoyment. In the fifth house the pair's Mercury turns conversation into recreation: banter, invented names for things, a running joke old enough to have its own history and long past explaining to anyone else. This relationship produces material. Very few pairs invent anything, and this one does it without setting out to. Subjects lean toward what delights: what to make, what to watch, what would be funny, what to try next. Ideas get chased because chasing them is fun and not because anything is meant to come of it. The pair talks about pleasure openly and without embarrassment, including its own. Creative work becomes shared property in the talking. The two of you will talk each other's projects into existence, or at least into a state where existing is possible. Enthusiasm is easy to raise here and easy to raise again after it fades, which is the useful half of it. Play is also how disagreement gets handled. An argument turns into a performance of the argument, exaggerated on both sides until it collapses into laughing, and the actual complaint sometimes collapses with it. If children are anywhere in this picture, and a chart says nothing about whether they are, they show up in the talk constantly: what one of them said, what to do about the school, the close commentary of a life being watched. The limit is that the format prefers to be entertaining. A subject that cannot be made light has trouble holding the room. Something serious gets a moment of genuine attention and is then set aside by a joke arriving a little too promptly, and both are relieved when it does. This pair gets very good at the recovery and stays less practised at sitting still. The unfunny conversation waits somewhere behind the funny one, unattended and in no hurry.

Schedules, lists, and who is collecting what: the running of things is where this pair's talk keeps landing. A sixth-house Mercury makes the relationship's conversation operational. There is always something to sort out, and sorting it out together takes up a good part of the attention these two give each other. The exchange is useful. Arrangements get made properly, times get confirmed, and the practical business of two lives that touch is handled without much drama. Work is a standing subject: what happened at it, what is coming, how to deal with the person who is making it difficult. Daily upkeep comes up too, in the plain way people mention what they ate and whether they slept. Correction lives in this register. Noticing an inefficiency and mentioning it come out as a single gesture here. It runs in both directions, and both of you get corrected more by each other than by anyone outside. Most of it is meant helpfully. Some of it accumulates all the same, and the pile of small remarks ends up heavier than anything either would say outright. Care arrives as a task. When something is wrong, this pair reaches for what can be done: who to call, what would help, what to try first. That is affection in a working dialect, and it is not always the dialect the moment asked for. What has no place in the format is the conversation with nothing to accomplish. Idle talk feels like time spent badly, so it gets cut short, and the relationship can run a long stretch with everything handled and very little said. The handled part is not nothing. It is simply narrower than what talking can do, and the pair notices the narrowness on the days when there is nothing left on the list.

What these two discuss most is the arrangement itself. Mercury in the seventh of the composite turns the pair's talk toward terms: what each expects, what was agreed, what counts as fair, what one of them believed the other had understood. This relationship negotiates out loud, and it does it continually. The result is unusual clarity about the deal. Little runs on assumption. Where other bonds find out after five years that each had a different idea of what this was, these two have said it, more than once, and can quote the conversation back. Explicit agreements are easier to keep than implied ones, and this pair makes them explicit by reflex. The two also talk as a unit to everyone else. Facing an institution, a difficult relative, a person who has made a mistake that has to be corrected: they prepare, decide who says what, and go in with a position. Third parties are frequent subjects, and so is the question of how the pair is being treated by them. The recurring hazard is meta. A conversation about the conversation can quietly replace the thing the conversation was about. Two hours go on how something was said and the something never gets addressed. Both of you may recognise the particular tiredness of an evening spent entirely on the terms of an argument that never began. This is the house people arrive at carrying the one question they actually want settled, so it is worth being direct about the limit. Nothing in a composite reports on duration. The placement describes what the talking is preoccupied with, which is the bond taken as an agreement between two people. Whether that agreement gets kept is not information a chart holds.

The subjects here are the ones most people keep off the table. The eighth house pulls this pair's conversation toward what is owed, what is shared and cannot be divided, what was done to one of them years ago and never explained. Between these two, the private thing gets said out loud. Joint matters are constant: debts, obligations, what belongs to both rather than to either, arrangements that would be awkward to describe to a third person. Money appears here as entanglement rather than as budget: not what things cost, but who is carrying what, and what the carrying means. The pair works those questions over in detail and does not tire of them. Talk also goes after motive. What someone actually meant, why a person behaved that way, what sits under a story that does not add up: this is the pair's favourite kind of problem. They investigate together and they are often right. They also build long theories about people out of small evidence, hold them with more confidence than the evidence supports, and rarely check them with anyone outside. Nothing much stays light. A remark meant in passing gets picked up and examined, and a subject that would be minor elsewhere gains weight here simply by being discussed at this depth. Secrets are kept well between these two, including from each other, and the two of you may each be carrying something that has still never come up. Loss and the things that end are ordinary subjects rather than forbidden ones. Most people have nowhere at all to say those sentences aloud. The cost sits on the same page as the benefit: a conversation that goes down this fast has trouble coming back up, and the small talk gets converted into something heavier before it has finished being small.

What this pair discusses tends to sit some distance from where they are standing. A ninth-house Mercury sends the talk outward: another country, another century, a principle instead of the instance in front of them. These two think together at range, and they enjoy the range. Belief is an ordinary subject. What is right, what things mean, how a person ought to live: these come up on a Tuesday rather than only in a crisis, and both take them seriously without either needing to win. The relationship has an appetite for the large question and is comfortable leaving one open, which most conversations are not. Travel gets talked about constantly, whether or not any of it happens. So does study. When either takes up something new to learn, it becomes joint property in the talking, explained across a table until both know the outline of a subject only one of them is actually doing. Distant places, languages, law, history: this is the natural material. Disagreement here is usually about principle rather than about conduct. It stays civil that way, and it runs long. An argument about what is fair in general can run for weeks without either of them mentioning the specific thing that started it. There is a great deal of theory in the bond. Talk reaches the general fast and prefers to stay there. A concrete difficulty comes in and gets answered with a principle, and the principle is often sound, and it still does not say who is collecting the parcel on Thursday. So the relationship can be extremely well furnished with ideas and short on the small settled facts that keep two lives running alongside each other. The gap is not inattention. It is where the attention goes by default. What the two of you say at this range is worth having, and it works better with a narrower conversation running behind it, doing the arithmetic.

The world outside is where this talk keeps arriving. The tenth house sets the pair's conversation on standing, work, and how the bond looks from a distance. These two discuss their position, and they discuss it often. Ambition is a shared subject. What comes next, what a move would cost in reputation, whether something was handled well where people could see: this is ordinary content here. Careers get talked through in detail, and the relationship functions partly as an advisory body. Each is a first reader for the other, and the advice is usually good, because both have spent time thinking about how things look from outside. The pair also has a public voice. What both of you say in front of other people tends to be consistent, either worked out beforehand or arrived at so often that it no longer needs working out. Other people know where this relationship stands. The bond acquires a reputation of its own, and these two are aware of the reputation and talk about that too. Harder is the unimpressive private sentence. A register this alert to appearances struggles with the admission that has no upside, so confusion tends to get reported after it has been resolved rather than while it is happening. Each may be more candid with a stranger on a train than with the other. What loosens that is one unpolished report, given while the problem is still a problem, and the advisory body gets better at its actual work every time one of those is allowed through.

Other people are in the room even when they are not. An eleventh-house Mercury places the pair's talk among the circle around them: friends, the group, who is in and who has drifted, what somebody did and what it means for everyone else. This relationship keeps a running account of its social world, and the account is detailed. The register is friendly whatever the relationship actually is. These two talk like allies rather than like parties to a negotiation, and there is a lightness in it that survives serious content. Ideas get traded instead of defended. Either can float something half-formed and have it taken seriously, which is less common than it sounds. The future is the other standing subject, and it arrives in the plural: what could be done, what the two might join or start or belong to, how things ought to be arranged for everyone. Plans here are collective by instinct: a trip becomes a group trip, a project acquires other people, an idea gets an audience before it gets a second draft. Disagreements often get outsourced. A view is tested on a friend before it is put to the other person, and news about the pair sometimes travels through the circle before it travels between them. The talk works best with some company in it, real or remembered. Put these two alone in a room with nothing external to discuss and the conversation can go oddly quiet. There is a version of this bond that knows everything about everyone it knows and remains a stranger to itself. That is not coldness. The subject with no third party in it simply arrives last, after everything else has been dealt with, and it waits until both of you are somewhere with nobody else to talk about.

A good deal of this relationship's thinking never becomes a sentence. The twelfth house keeps the pair's talk partly underground, in the part of the chart that holds what is private, unfinished, or set aside. Things are understood without being stated. Things are also avoided without anyone deciding to avoid them. Much of the exchange happens where nobody can see it. The real conversations occur late, or in waiting rooms and airports and other places where the ordinary rules are suspended, or not aloud at all. In company these two may say very little to each other and still be in constant communication. Anything without a hard edge moves easily: dreams, half-memories, a feeling about a person that neither can source, the thought that was never finished. There is genuine understanding in it. Each can often tell what the other is thinking, and neither has to perform the explanation ordinary talk requires. What gets deferred is the plain statement. A difficult subject can be circled for months and then dissolve without ever being addressed, and both may privately count the dissolving as resolution. Sometimes it is. Sometimes it is a thing put in a drawer. The drawers in this house are deep, and neither of you tends to be the one who opens them.
